results.reason: Issue 1 identifies that §9.4(c) removes the 10% cap for every §9.2(a) claim, not only Fundamental Representations. It explains the resulting uncapped exposure beyond the escrow and recommends narrowing the carve-out to Fundamental Representations and fraud.

Issue 3 identifies the Delaware law and forum in TSA §9.3 and the conflict with New York. It explains that §10.12 lets the TSA control its own subject matter, so the conflict is not cured. It notes the risk of split, parallel proceedings and proposes New York replacement language.

Issue 2 identifies that Bill of Sale §1.1(b) covers all assets 'used or held for use in the Business' with no carve-out or cross-reference to the APA. It explains that the Bill of Sale controls under §10.12 and could convey retained assets. It recommends adopting the APA definition with an express exclusion of the Excluded Assets.
The memo states the cap is 10% of the Purchase Price, or $1,840,000 on $18,400,000, and notes this equals the Escrow Amount.
The memo names Seller's cash, the Albany manufacturing facility and the HOLLIS trademark as Excluded Assets.
The deliverable is in memo format. Each issue has a Document/Section heading, a 'Why it matters to Marrowind' discussion and a 'Recommended fix'.
Issues are listed 'in order of significance' with the most significant first. Part IV is a separate section for items requiring a client business decision.
The memo expressly states that §10.12 does not cure Issues 2 or 3.
The memo states that neither the 10% cap nor the escrow limits liability for ordinary representation breaches.
